findings.description: mark_invalid appends the marker to the file for impression.served_at.date(), and for_day only looks for markers in the same day file. This works if served_at is the same value that append used. But append and for_day bucket by served_at.date() in the datetime's own timezone, while pacing buckets by hour using the same naive/aware value. If a refund arrives with an impression whose served_at differs (for example, reconstructed in another timezone), the marker lands in a different day file and the original impression keeps counting against the budget.
findings.suggestion: Look up the original record's day or normalise served_at to a single timezone (e.g. UTC) in append, mark_invalid and for_day.
findings.title: Invalid markers written to the file of the served day, which can differ from the day read

findings.description: can_bid now calls spend(), which opens and JSON-parses the whole day's log file for each campaign on every bid request. eligible() does this for every campaign, so a bid request costs O(campaigns x log size). The log grows through the day, so latency on the hot bidding path increases steadily, and reads are not cached.
findings.suggestion: Keep an in-memory per-day, per-campaign hourly aggregate, loaded from the log once at startup and updated on record/refund.
findings.title: Whole day file re-read and parsed on every bid check
